name: WA-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: DelBene's massive financial advantage ($3.55M raised vs ~$3K)
Incumbent seeking re-election with no serious outside opposition
model.rationale: DelBene holds a D+15 district, has out-raised her opponent by more than a thousand to one, and faces no outside spending or polling suggesting competition; markets price her win at roughly 95%. The fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit Democratic margin.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against DelBene or an unusually strong Republican top-of-ticket environment in Washington could narrow the margin, though a seat flip remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Suzan DelBene, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking re-election in a Seattle-area district that leans Democratic by about fifteen points. She advanced to the general election against Republican Mary Silva, a first-time challenger with minimal resources. DelBene has raised over $3.5 million and holds more than $1.1 million on hand, while Silva has raised only a few thousand dollars, leaving a staggering financial gap.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, and no outside groups are spending against the incumbent. Prediction markets give DelBene roughly a 95 percent chance of winning. With the incumbent's advantages in money, name recognition, and district lean all pointing the same direction, this seat is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty limited to the size of the winning margin rather than the outcome.
